package_info.package_versions: Multiple; at least eleven distinct applications as of July 2020
package_info.why_malicious: The Joker malware family is an infostealer and ad clicker that uses obfuscation and staged payload delivery to evade detection, steal sensitive user data, and perform unauthorized actions such as premium SMS fraud and ad fraud.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after app launch, often after staged delay)
execution_context.file_location: Obfuscated Java/Kotlin code within the APK (e.g., MainActivity or background service)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads SMS messages and contact data, then exfiltrates this information to a command-and-control server, and attempts to subscribe the user to premium services via silent SMS, resulting in data theft and financial fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing SMS, contacts, and sending data to external servers is highly suspicious for a benign app, especially when combined with premium service subscription.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal currency converter or utility apps should not access SMS or contacts, nor communicate with unknown servers or subscribe users to paid services.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some messaging or backup apps may access SMS/contacts, but only with clear user consent and without exfiltration to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Obfuscated code to hide malicious logic
Access to SMS and contacts without clear user purpose

execution_context.trigger: runtime (background service, often after staged update)
execution_context.file_location: Downloaded payload (DEX file) loaded dynamically after app update

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app downloads an additional DEX payload from a remote server, loads it dynamically, and executes further malicious logic, enabling modular and evolving attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic code loading from external sources is a common evasion and persistence technique in Android malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not download and execute code at runtime from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some apps may update modules/plugins, but only from trusted, verified sources and with user awareness.
key_indicators: Network requests to C2 for code updates
Execution of code not present in original APK

attack_chain.action: User installs a seemingly benign app from Google Play Store.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial app execution and permission requests

attack_chain.action: App requests sensitive permissions (SMS, contacts, etc.) under false pretenses.
App executes obfuscated malicious logic to access SMS, contacts, and other sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration and premium service subscription

attack_chain.action: App downloads and loads additional malicious payloads from C2 infrastructure to extend or update malicious capabilities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continued data theft, ad fraud, or further malicious actions

behavioral_signatures: Android app accessing SMS and contacts without clear user purpose
Dynamic loading of DEX files from remote servers
Silent subscription to premium SMS services
Obfuscated code and staged payload delivery
file_indicators: Presence of obfuscated classes and methods in APK
Dynamic loading of secondary DEX files
Unusual permissions in manifest (READ_SMS, SEND_SMS, READ_CONTACTS)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Joker C2 domains/IPs
Unusual POST requests containing SMS/contact data
Download of executable code (DEX) after installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Android apps for access to SMS and contacts, dynamic code loading behavior, and network connections to known malicious infrastructure. Flag apps that request sensitive permissions without clear justification, especially if they communicate with external servers or attempt to subscribe users to premium services. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect obfuscated code and staged payload delivery.
